screens.name: Home — available omen, 390/430px, Chrome/WebKit

screens.name: Home — omen loading

screens.name: Home — unavailable omen and collapsed daily limit

screens.name: Home — expanded daily-limit policy and constrained height

screens.name: Question entry — approach and input-method choice
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4, 36 and 58 show a centered orb, 'Your question,' and distinct typing and speaking actions with corresponding transition captures.

screens.name: Question composer — self, named person and populated drafts
screens.evidence: Sheets 4–6, 16, 56 and 58 show labeled populated fields and explicit submission, with draft and focus preservation reported.
findings: Shorten the enlarged provider-purpose explanation so the question remains the dominant task content.

screens.name: Question composer — constrained height and long text
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–38 show internally scrolling question fields and reachable submission at simulated 500px height.

screens.name: Named-person selection — populated and selected
screens.evidence: Sheet 5 shows Someone selected, the labeled Alex field, a privacy explanation and explicit 'Use this person' action.
findings: Keep Cancel changes readily discoverable at 200% text after the primary action.

screens.name: Voice entry — startup failure and typing fallback
screens.evidence: Sheets 38 and 58 show microphone startup failure with typing as the primary recovery and voice retry as a secondary action.
findings: Reduce the enlarged decorative heading so the failure explanation appears sooner.

screens.name: Adaptive questions — unselected first, middle and final cards
screens.evidence: Sheets 7–9, 55 and 61 show question, progress, radio choices and disabled Continue or Reveal, with keyboard and target checks reported.
findings: Preserve this compact question-first structure for generated questions with longer answer labels.

screens.name: Adaptive questions — selected, keyboard-focused and retained answers
screens.evidence: Sheets 3, 10, 24–26 and 62 show distinct selection and focus, while runtime evidence reports explicit commitment, restoration and single submission.
findings: Retain the separate selection and commitment states across all future question variants.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty and populated
screens.evidence: Sheets 9 and 36 show the complete question, persistent answer label, Back to choices and disabled or enabled submission.
findings: Clarify the different destinations of the top back arrow and Back to choices without requiring users to try them.

screens.name: Custom answer — constrained viewport and long response
screens.evidence: Sheet 37 shows the complete question and Reveal preserved while a long response scrolls inside a shortened field.
findings: Improve the field's scroll affordance and keep navigation retrievable without ambiguous nested scrolling.

screens.name: Age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheet 39 shows explicit older/younger choices and explains that omitted birthdays use limits for ages 13–17.
findings: Replace 'Readings use the limits for ages 13–17' with a plain explanation of what those limits mean to the user.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday
screens.evidence: Sheets 39–40 show optionality and Skip beside labeled birthday inputs, with stacked year at 200% and validation checks reported.

screens.name: Age blocked — onboarding and birthday editor

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday correction
screens.evidence: Sheet 41 shows actual-birthday guidance, labeled fields and Check birthday, with eligibility correction verified in runtime evidence.
findings: Keep the return to the age requirement easy to discover after the enlarged form.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional focus, unselected and selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 2 and 42–43 show optional focus choices, a check-marked selection and the primary action changing from Skip focus to Meet the Ball.

screens.name: Birthday editor — populated
screens.evidence: Sheet 79 shows populated date fields, Save birthday, Cancel changes and collapsed removal, with save/reload and unchanged cancellation reported.

screens.name: Birthday editor — invalid date and partial draft

screens.name: Birth city — empty search
screens.evidence: Sheets 77–78 show a labeled city field, disabled search and a concise explanation of the lookup provider and transmitted data.

screens.name: Birth chart — calculated result
screens.evidence: Sheet 55 shows Moon/rising results, local-save confirmation, city/time context and edit/forget actions.

screens.name: Planning and research — loading
screens.evidence: Sheets 53–54, 59 and 62–63 show stage-specific explanations, wait expectations and Cancel, with cancellation preserving readings reported.

screens.name: Recovery — extended wait

screens.name: Safety redirection — general and support-link variants

screens.name: Forecast opening — normal, golden, skip and reduced-motion paths
screens.evidence: Sheets 43–48 show charge/fracture/settled states, with measured motion, reduced-opacity paths, interruption and single-save checks reported.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — settled and early-share return
screens.evidence: Sheets 43–48 and 65–66 show stable forecast, qualifier, reminder and actions, with no replay on share return reported.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — expanded additional actions
screens.evidence: Sheets 63–64 show reminders, plans, question editing and answer review grouped under More actions.

screens.name: Evidence overview — Behind the mist

screens.name: Evidence — answers, including original-question labels
screens.evidence: Sheets 15, 21–22 and 56 show long fixture answers and real-flow details labeled with original questions or generic answer numbers.

screens.name: Evidence — assumptions
screens.evidence: Sheets 16, 22 and 55 show both long assumption fixtures and a real-flow Assumptions page containing only a generic speculative disclaimer.
findings: When no specific assumption exists, say so directly instead of presenting the general disclaimer as an assumption.

screens.name: Evidence — legacy reason passages
screens.evidence: Sheets 17, 23 and 65–66 show long reason text separated under neutral Passage labels, which runtime evidence identifies as preserved legacy content.

screens.name: Evidence — authored short Why and Plus entry

screens.name: Evidence — background sources

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: Home and opening sheets establish the illustrated orb as the hero, with motion performance, skip and reduced-motion paths reported.
findings: Make its actionable role equally evident to keyboard users and users who do not interpret decorative imagery as a control.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Home, Sky, History and You show consistent labeled tabs with gold active states and a raised Ask orb.
findings: Increase the normal-size label legibility while maintaining enough content clearance above the raised center orb.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Across sheets the fixed graphic wordmark remains stable while the reading balance enlarges and sometimes wraps to two lines.
findings: Give the balance a clearer control affordance if it opens plans, rather than relying on its thin underline.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: Cream buttons consistently distinguish primary actions, with visible disabled/busy variants and reported target, contrast and keyboard checks.
findings: Preserve the strong enabled/disabled distinction and keep long enlarged labels concise.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold text actions recur across forms, recovery and disclosures, with one visible rectangular keyboard-focus treatment.
findings: Standardize arrow, chevron and underline conventions so navigation, disclosure and immediate actions are easier to distinguish.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Question sheets show radio, gold selection and a distinct focus outline, supported by explicit-commit and native keyboard behavior tests.
findings: Retain the redundant radio and color indicators rather than making selection depend on gold alone.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Composer sheets show persistent labels, readable populated values and prominent focus borders.
findings: Keep disclosure text compact enough that the field remains the main visual task at enlarged text.

components.name: Large-text input
components.evidence: Sheets 37–38 show doubled input text, shortened fields and internal scrolling in constrained-height browser captures.
findings: Strengthen internal scroll cues and prove comfortable movement between field content and page context.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheet 68 shows readable switch labels and visually distinct on/off positions, while aggregate target measurements are reported.
findings: Show focused and announced switch states and verify persistence individually.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Home sheets show available, loading and unavailable omen content with next-attempt and policy variants.
findings: Keep the used-attempt explanation visible in the unavailable state without requiring expansion.

components.name: Sky stars and selected question
components.evidence: Sky sheets show a selected star theme and sample question, with a two-column text layout at 200%.
findings: Keep selection and its resulting question within a shorter visual span in the enlarged layout.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Circles captures expose offline and unsuccessful-retry states without implying that social setup is available.
findings: Reduce promotional emphasis until connection recovery succeeds.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: History captures separate date, question, forecast, reminder or outcome and check-in action with restrained dividers.
findings: Ensure each enlarged row presents a discoverable check-in action before becoming an extended reading block.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Plan captures distinguish selection with a check and gold divider while showing total price and billing cadence.
findings: Keep the total billed amount prominent when the option stacks vertically at 200%.

components.name: Share preview card
components.evidence: Share sheets show a branded portrait card with speculative labeling plus enlarged inspection and separate text access.
findings: Increase the small preview's qualifier legibility while preserving the complete downloadable composition.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Failure, timeout, safety and export sheets show specific recovery actions and contextual status messages.
findings: Apply consistent preserved-data and preserved-credit reassurance across equivalent failures.

components.name: Typography system
components.evidence: The sheets consistently pair serif headings with sans-serif controls and demonstrate 200% reflow with reported contrast measurements.
findings: Reduce repetitive enlarged introductory text and improve small normal-size metadata rather than enlarging every visual role equally.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: Dark mist and warm lower-page glow persist across transitions, with contrast and ambient-motion measurements reported.
findings: Keep stronger mist contours away from dense reason text and interactive boundaries.

components.name: Birthday input group
components.evidence: Birthday sheets preserve explicit day/month/year labels and reflow year to a full row at 200%, with invalid-draft tests reported.
findings: Associate each visible error with the specific field needing correction.

components.name: Age confirmation control
components.evidence: The age screen provides explicit older/younger choices and runtime evidence reports enforcement without a skip bypass.
findings: Explain the consequence of proceeding without a birthday in clearer user-facing language.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Focus sheets show spacious options, a check-marked selected row and explicit skip or completion actions.
findings: Preserve explicit completion and the visible ability to skip.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: You and chart-result sheets expose birth-derived details, local storage and edit/forget controls.
findings: Make missing-detail and age-fallback explanations as direct as the populated profile labels.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: Birth-detail sheets show optional time and city steps, format guidance and provider disclosure.
findings: Provide an explicit unknown-time exit and demonstrate city results and recovery states.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Named-person sheets show a checked subject choice, persistent first-name label and a clear no-notification explanation.
findings: Use a more explicit summary action such as 'Change person' instead of the generic 'change' suffix.

components.name: Evidence disclosure
components.evidence: Forecast and evidence sheets show chevrons, expanded content and separate overview destinations.
findings: Differentiate expansion from navigation consistently and avoid competing return/read-forecast controls.

components.name: Export status
components.evidence: Held, completed and recovery captures distinguish preparing, download started and failed export, supported by actual encoding and retry evidence.
findings: Verify live announcement of export state changes while leaving keyboard focus stable.

components.name: Permission modal
components.evidence: Consent captures show the provider-purpose disclosure and grant/decline choices, with constrained-height reachability and no-request permission checks reported.
findings: Make the grant label explicitly name the AI processing permission.

components.name: Outcome selection and save group
components.evidence: Outcome sheets show all three choices, enabled/disabled saving and explicit saved status, with keyboard and persistence checks reported.
findings: Use state-specific helper text for initial, unsaved and saved states.

limitations: All scores are provisional browser assessments based on the supplied sheets and runtime narrative; I did not execute or independently reproduce the reported checks.

Corresponding normal, enlarged, transition and repeated fixture captures are grouped by screen/state; still frames support visual continuity assessment but cannot independently prove animation timing or interaction.
For each item, A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; null dimensions are excluded, and overall is round(0.4A + 0.6F, 1).

The requested A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across all screens and components; several selection controls reach it provisionally, but forms, evidence presentation, secondary navigation and state copy do not.
No definite hard-gate failure is established by this material; viewport-edge cropping alone does not establish unreachable content, particularly where scrolling is reported.
Physical iPhone Dynamic Type, real keyboard behavior, VoiceOver, native haptics, microphone hardware and native sharing remain unverified and are not certified by these browser grades.
The 500px captures simulate constrained height; they do not prove native keyboard avoidance or focus behavior.
Supabase-backed authenticated social behavior, real payments and actual external named-provider processing are not demonstrated.
Synthetic layout text and test-provider labels were treated as intentional fixtures, not production-copy defects or evidence of model quality.
City search results/failures, complete invitation/reminder outcomes and individual settings announcement/persistence states lack sufficient pictured evidence.
Reported contrast, target sizes, axe results and browser performance strengthen the assessment but do not establish repeated novice success or full assistive-technology usability.
topFixes: Use state-specific check-in guidance: initial selection, unsaved change and saved confirmation should say different things.
When specific assumptions are unavailable, state that directly instead of showing a generic disclaimer as an assumption.
Reduce enlarged explanatory copy and clarify nested scrolling in constrained composer and custom-answer views.
Standardize secondary navigation, disclosure symbols and focus treatments, especially duplicate back controls and blue heading outlines.
Make unavailable-omen policy and unknown-birth-time exits explicit without requiring inference.
Complete browser evidence for city-search recovery, invite/reminder outcomes and announced status changes, then perform the deferred physical accessibility pass.
